fields.meta_title: Trip Report Form Builder, Free to Start | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a trip report form that records why each trip happened and what it found, sends follow-ups to their owners and reminds late filers.
fields.h1: Build a Trip Report Form Every Traveler Files the Same Way
fields.hero_description: Build a trip report form that captures the purpose and findings of every trip, with each follow-up assigned to an owner.
fields.features_heading: What a Trip Report Should Bring Home
fields.features_subheading: Reports written a week late lose names and decisions. Describe the trips you take, and Emergent builds the form and its database.
fields.feature_1:
Sections in the order a reader needs

The form asks for the reason for the trip, then what the traveler found, then the conclusions. Your manager reads the outcome without hunting through a page of travel notes.
fields.feature_2:
Follow-ups that carry a name and a date

Each conclusion can become a task with an owner and a due date. The owner gets an email with the task, and the report shows which follow-ups are still open a week later.
fields.feature_3:
Receipts photographed into the report

Photograph a fuel or hotel receipt, and the app reads the merchant, date, and total into fields. Any value it cannot read clearly goes back to the traveler to type in.
fields.feature_4:
A reminder for every late report

Set a filing deadline counted in days from the return date. Anyone past it gets an email reminder, and the team lead sees which reports are in and which are still missing.
fields.feature_5:
Every trip on file in one place

Each report saves to a database you own, so you can look up every visit to one client or every conference from last year. Filter the list by traveler or by the month of the trip.
fields.feature_6:
Your codebase on your own servers

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host it where your other internal tools run. Keep building on it from there, or keep changing it by prompt.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Files the Report, and Who Acts on It
fields.tab_content_1:
Each follow-up from the Pomfrey visit lands with its owner

Tabitha Crouchmore sells flow meters for Saxelby Instruments and spent Tuesday at Pomfrey Dairy's bottling plant. Her report says why she went and who she met, and it lists 3 follow-ups. Each task reaches the person named on it by email. Jessamine Wrexcombe, her sales manager, reads the report that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_2:
Ten days after returning, any missing report gets a reminder

Drewsbury County Library sends 4 staff to a 3-day state library conference. Each attendee lists sessions attended and uploads a certificate of completion. No report 10 days after the return date means an email reminder. This year Wystan Dimmock got one, and director Dorcas Ellerbeck saw the other 3 were in.
fields.tab_content_3:
Every fuel receipt read into gallons and dollars

Hartwyn Freight drivers file a trip report after each run, with miles by state. Petronella Tiverton logged 546 miles on run 2207. Her photo of a Cinderford Fuel receipt filled in 96.4 gallons and $351.86. The app could not read the smudged date, so it asked her to type it before the report saved.
fields.tab_content_4:
When anything goes wrong on a trip, the principal hears

Teachers at Ulmscott Middle School file a report after every field trip, with headcounts and anything that went wrong. Clementine Mapplethorpe took 52 students to the science museum, and all 52 returned, but the bus home left 35 minutes late. A listed incident emails the principal, Anselm Trowbridge, the same day.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Trip Report Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a trip report form that records every trip in one shape and puts each follow-up in front of its owner.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List the trips your people take
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Open with who went, where, and why
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Turn each conclusion into a task
fields.howto_step_1_des: Look back at last quarter's travel: client visits, conferences, delivery runs, school outings. Each kind of trip gets its own set of questions. A driver never sees the conference fields, and a teacher never scrolls past mileage.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask for the traveler, the destination, the dates, and the reason for the trip at the top. Someone who opens the report a year from now should know what the trip was for in two lines.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give what the traveler found its own box, and the conclusions another. The MIT writing guide names both as parts of a trip report. Split this way, a manager can skim the conclusions and read the detail only when a decision depends on it.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a follow-up list under the conclusions. Each row names a task and the person who owns it, plus a due date. Email that person when the report is filed, and keep open tasks on the report until someone marks them done.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Collect the paperwork inside the form
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add upload fields for whatever a trip produces, such as fuel receipts, hotel folios, certificates of completion, or a signed attendance sheet. Receipt photos can fill amounts into fields, and the traveler checks anything the app could not read.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set a deadline and a reminder
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick a filing window counted from the return date, for example 5 working days. Email a reminder to anyone past it. Give the team lead one page that shows which reports have come in and whose are still outstanding.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test with a real trip, then share it
fields.howto_step_7_des: File one report from a recent trip before anyone else sees the form. Confirm each follow-up email reached its owner and every receipt amount came through right. Then send the link to the people who travel.

faq_plan.q: What is a trip report form?
faq_plan.a: A trip report form is a set of fields an employee fills in after work travel, recording who went, where, why, and what came of it. The MIT writing guide says trip reports should include the reason for the trip, what was found, and one or more conclusions.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a trip report form?
faq_plan.a: Describe your trips to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English: who travels, what they should record, and who reads the report. Emergent builds the form, its database, and the follow-up emails, and you change any of it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a trip report form have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short enough to finish in 10 minutes on a phone. Open with who traveled and why, give findings and conclusions a box each, and add a follow-up list. Put questions for one kind of trip behind a trip type. Then nobody answers fields that do not apply.

faq_plan.q: Should a trip report form ask about problems during the trip?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Note each problem in a sentence or two, such as a missed meeting or a vehicle breakdown, and what was done about it. An injury or property damage needs its own incident report form, filed separately so it reaches the person who handles it.

faq_plan.q: When should employees fill out a trip report form?
faq_plan.a: Set a window your travelers can meet, such as 5 working days after the return date, and hold everyone to it. The form Emergent builds can send late filers a reminder email and show the team lead who has not filed yet.

faq_plan.q: Can travelers attach receipts to a trip report form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an upload field, and travelers can photograph each receipt from a phone. Apps built with Emergent can also read each receipt's amount and date into the report and flag any value they are unsure of for the traveler to confirm.

faq_plan.q: What should a field trip report form for teachers include?
faq_plan.a: Record the destination, how many students left and how many returned, the chaperones, and anything that went wrong, plus a line on what the class learned. A field trip permission slip covers the trip before it happens, and the report is the record afterward.

faq_plan.q: Who should receive a completed trip report form?
faq_plan.a: Send it to the traveler's manager and to everyone who owns a follow-up from it. For a conference, share it with the colleagues who stayed behind as well. The app Emergent builds keeps each report in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up a trip report form for conference attendees?
faq_plan.a: Ask for the two takeaways the team should act on first, then the sessions attended and one line on what each changed. Add an upload field for slides and handouts so nobody retypes them, and end with the follow-ups.

faq_plan.q: Is a trip report form the same as an expense report?
faq_plan.a: No. A trip report records what a trip achieved and what happens next. An expense report claims back what the trip cost, line by line with receipts. Keep them as separate forms that share a trip ID. The expense report form can then pull the dates and destination from the trip report.

plan.angle: The results for this query are printable trip report templates (Visme, Venngage, Word and PDF downloads) and one form-tool template page. They stop at the blank fields. None shows a report that does something after it is filed: follow-ups that reach their owners, a reminder when a conference report is late, fuel receipts read into the report, an incident on a school trip that reaches the principal. This page shows a working trip report form for four kinds of trips, with every report saved to a database the organization owns, and states the trip report structure only as the MIT writing guide gives it.
